body:
Group photo with Kyushu University students

On August 12, 2024, the Environmental Engineering and Agricultural Building Laboratory, Department of Agricultural Engineering, Faculty of Agricultural Technology UGM, received a special visit from 13 students from Kyushu University, Japan, accompanied by Assoc. Prof. Takahiro Fujiwara, Ph.D. This visit aimed to introduce the students to the Smart Agriculture research facilities and observe firsthand the Indoor Farming – Smart Agri Plant Factory.

The delegation was warmly welcomed by Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho, who is also an alumnus of Kyushu University, having completed his doctoral program in 2016. In his welcome remarks, Dr. Andri expressed his hope that this visit would provide deep insights into the facilities and current research at the Smart Agriculture Research Center, which is located in the Environmental Engineering and Agricultural Building Laboratory (TLBP).

![](/brand/uploads/notes/140-1-kunjungan-kyushu-university-smart-agri2-1024x740.webp)

Presentation of the TLBP Laboratory

![](/brand/uploads/notes/140-2-kunjungan-kyushu-university-smart-agri-1024x765.webp)

Discussion on research at Lab. TLBP

Prof. Fujiwara explained that this visit was part of a series of Summer Course events organized by the Faculty of Forestry UGM. Given that some students have a background in Agricultural Engineering, they were invited to learn more about Smart Farming and Precision Agriculture at the Faculty of Agricultural Technology.

During the visit, the students were taken on a tour to view research posters and research equipment at the Smart Agri Plant Factory. Discussions about various possibilities for future collaboration were also an important part of the visit. The hope is that this visit will open opportunities for cooperation in the field of precision agriculture and strengthen the relationship between the two universities.

This visit highlighted the importance of agricultural productivity and innovation in addressing global food security challenges. By establishing partnerships in research and development, both UGM and Kyushu University aim to contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly in the field of sustainable agriculture and food systems.

In addition to the tour, the students also participated in interactive sessions where they interacted with researchers and research students. This allowed them to gain a deeper understanding of ongoing projects and the impact of smart agricultural technology on increasing agricultural productivity.

Collaboration between UGM and Kyushu University is expected to result in joint research initiatives, student exchange programs, and knowledge sharing in the field of agricultural engineering. Such partnerships are vital in advancing sustainable agriculture goals and ensuring food security amid climate change and population growth.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/140-3-kunjungan-kyushu-university-smart-agriculture--1024x714.webp)

Presentation of souvenirs by representatives of Kyushu University students

As the world continues to face food production challenges, initiatives such as this visit play an important role in educating the next generation of agricultural engineers and researchers. By working together, universities can leverage their strengths to develop innovative solutions that benefit local and global communities.

In conclusion, the visit of Kyushu University students to UGM marks a significant step toward increased collaboration in smart agriculture. It is evidence of both institutions' commitment to improving agricultural productivity and contributing to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals.

original.body:
Foto bersama dengan Mahasiswa Kyushu University

Pada tanggal 12 Agustus 2024, Laboratorium Teknik Lingkungan dan Bangunan Pertanian, Departemen Teknik Pertanian, Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian UGM, menerima kunjungan istimewa dari 13 mahasiswa Kyushu University, Jepang, yang didampingi oleh Asoc. Prof. Takahiro Fujiwara, Ph.D. Kunjungan ini bertujuan untuk memperkenalkan para mahasiswa pada fasilitas riset Smart Agriculture dan mengamati langsung Indoor Farming – Smart Agri Plant Factory.

Rombongan disambut hangat oleh Dr. Andri Prima Nugroho yang juga alumni Kyushu University menyelesaikan program doktoralnya pada tahun 2016. Dalam sambutannya, Dr. Andri menyampaikan harapannya agar kunjungan ini dapat memberikan wawasan mendalam mengenai fasilitas dan penelitian terkini di Smart Agriculture Research Center yang berlokasi di Laboratorium Teknik Lingkungan dan Bangunan Pertanian (TLBP).

![](/brand/uploads/notes/140-1-kunjungan-kyushu-university-smart-agri2-1024x740.webp)

Penjelasan Laboratorium TLBP

![](/brand/uploads/notes/140-2-kunjungan-kyushu-university-smart-agri-1024x765.webp)

Diskusi tentang penelitian di Lab. TLBP

Prof. Fujiwara menjelaskan bahwa kunjungan ini merupakan bagian dari rangkaian acara Summer Course yang diselenggarakan oleh Fakultas Kehutanan UGM. Mengingat beberapa mahasiswa memiliki latar belakang Teknik Pertanian, mereka diajak untuk belajar lebih lanjut mengenai Smart Farming dan Pertanian Presisi di Fakultas Teknologi Pertanian.

Selama kunjungan, para mahasiswa diajak berkeliling untuk melihat poster-poster penelitian dan peralatan riset di Smart Agri Plant Factory. Diskusi mengenai berbagai kemungkinan kolaborasi di masa depan juga menjadi bagian penting dari kunjungan ini. Harapannya, kunjungan ini dapat membuka peluang kerjasama dalam bidang pertanian presisi dan mempererat hubungan antara kedua universitas.

Kunjungan ini menyoroti pentingnya produktivitas pertanian dan inovasi dalam menghadapi tantangan keamanan pangan global. Dengan menjalin kemitraan dalam riset dan pengembangan, baik UGM maupun Kyushu University bertujuan untuk berkontribusi pada Tujuan Pembangunan Berkelanjutan (SDGs), khususnya dalam bidang pertanian berkelanjutan dan sistem pangan.

Selain tur, para mahasiswa juga berpartisipasi dalam sesi interaktif di mana mereka berinteraksi dengan peneliti dan mahasiswa penelitian. Ini memungkinkan mereka untuk mendapatkan pemahaman yang lebih dalam tentang proyek-proyek yang sedang berlangsung dan dampak teknologi pertanian cerdas terhadap peningkatan produktivitas pertanian.

Kolaborasi antara UGM dan Kyushu University diharapkan dapat menghasilkan inisiatif riset bersama, program pertukaran mahasiswa, dan berbagi pengetahuan di bidang teknik pertanian. Kemitraan semacam ini sangat penting dalam memajukan tujuan pertanian berkelanjutan dan memastikan keamanan pangan di tengah perubahan iklim dan pertumbuhan populasi.

![](/brand/uploads/notes/140-3-kunjungan-kyushu-university-smart-agriculture--1024x714.webp)

Penyerahan Kenang – Kenangan oleh perwakilan mahasiswa Kyushu University

Seiring dunia terus menghadapi tantangan produksi pangan, inisiatif seperti kunjungan ini memainkan peran penting dalam mendidik generasi berikutnya dari insinyur dan peneliti pertanian. Dengan bekerja sama, universitas dapat memanfaatkan kekuatan mereka untuk mengembangkan solusi inovatif yang bermanfaat bagi komunitas lokal dan global.

Sebagai kesimpulan, kunjungan mahasiswa Kyushu University ke UGM menandai langkah signifikan menuju peningkatan kolaborasi dalam smart agriculture. Ini adalah bukti komitmen kedua institusi untuk meningkatkan produktivitas pertanian dan berkontribusi pada pencapaian Tujuan Pembangunan Berkelanjutan.
